$comment: Catalog of coding agents og knows how to wire into Omnigent.
Adding a vendor is a row here, not code. Fields:
id            stable key used in og-install.json state
label         what the picker shows
harness       the Omnigent harness id this agent runs on
binary        what `command -v` looks for during the scan
kind          native      -> Omnigent has a first-class harness with a
vendor TUI, hosted in a terminal pane
direct      -> a first-class harness Omnigent drives itself
(headless, no vendor TUI and no terminal tab)
acp-builtin -> Omnigent ships an ACP row for it
acp-user    -> needs an `acp.agents` entry in
~/.omnigent/config.yaml (og writes it)
acp_command   argv for acp-user kinds, e.g. 'cline --acp'
For acp-user kinds `harness` MUST be acp:<slug> where slug is
Omnigent's slugify(label): lowercase, non-alphanumerics -> '-'.
A wrong slug does not error — Omnigent silently falls back to
the FIRST configured acp.agents row, i.e. a different vendor.
roles         the slots this row has historically filled, INFORMATIONAL
only: it no longer gates any picker. Every detected agent is
offered for every role (orchestrator, coder, reviewer,
scout, integrator); whether it can ACTUALLY fill one is
decided by the measured dispatch probe (see `relay`) and
validate(). Kept so consumers that read it keep working.
unverified_roles  roles this agent is legal for but has NEVER been driven
in here, e.g. ["orchestrator"] — validate() still passes (the
row clears the role's gates), but the role is unproven, so
validate() warns, the picker flags the option, and
--questions carries the caveat. Distinct from the role-less
`unverified` flag, which condemns the WHOLE row in the
detected-CLI list — devin is a verified coder and unverified
only as an orchestrator. grok dropped `orchestrator` entirely
when it turned out incapable of dispatching.
roles_note    the human explanation behind `unverified_roles`; informational
only — the field code reads is `unverified_roles`.
vendor        model family, used for the cross-vendor review check.
Two agents sharing a vendor cannot review each other.
vendor_from_model_only  true when the provider family is knowable ONLY
from the model pin. For a multi-model harness (Pi), an
absent or unplaceable pin is treated as UNKNOWN, not as
the row's `vendor` placeholder: it might share any
provider, so the review check warns instead of claiming
a cross-vendor pairing it cannot prove.
model.required  true when a dispatch MUST pin a model. Unpinned
workers usually inherit the ORCHESTRATOR's model id,
which most harnesses cannot resolve.
model.required_reason  row-specific explanation for `required`, used
in the refusal when the pin is blank (e.g. Pi has no
model to inherit and its own fallback is not stable).
model.pin_path  where the pin goes in the sub-agent spec. Always
executor.model — executor.config is a free-form dict
and a model placed there is silently ignored.
model.list_cmd  argv for a live model probe. Default output parsing
accepts bare ids or a JSON array; set model.list_parser
when the id is in another column (pi_table reads the
MODEL column of Pi's provider-first table).
model.pinnable  false when the row must NOT offer a model pin at all
(default: true). Only claude sets it: pinning the
ORCHESTRATOR also pins the model family its workers
route within, which strands non-Claude workers. Never
combine with model.required — validate() refuses the pair,
since the worker would never be asked for the pin it needs.
relay         FALLBACK ONLY, used when Omnigent cannot be imported from
the installer's interpreter: false when the agent runs
without Omnigent's sys_* tool relay (leaf worker only;
cannot orchestrate). Superseded by the measured
`capabilities[<harness>].subagents` probe otherwise -- this
flag was wrong for six rows that claimed true while their
harness reports subagents=False.
silent_model_failure  true when a bad model id produces an empty
transcript instead of an error
worker        sub-agent name in the bundle. Defaults to coder_<id>; set it explicitly to keep an established name stable across an id change.

model.note: Subscription login picks the model. Pinning the ORCHESTRATOR also pins the family its workers route within, which strands non-Claude workers — leave it unset.

agents.label: OpenCode (Zen)

model.note: `opencode models` lists every provider you added with `opencode auth login` (deepseek/..., anthropic/...), not just Zen; those bill at the provider's rates, and a paid Zen id on a workspace with no payment method is a FAILED dispatch, not a slower one. Zen's free `opencode/*-free` lineup rotates, so verify `prefer` against `opencode models` rather than trusting it. Install from `anomalyco/tap/opencode` or npm's `opencode-ai` (both stay on 1.18), never plain `brew install opencode`: homebrew-core keeps ONE opencode formula and it is on 2.x, while the harness pins 1.17.7 <= v < 1.19.0 — and it reports that refusal as `version-too-low`, telling you to UPGRADE when you must DOWNGRADE.

agents.reviewer_warning: Zen's free lineup rotates, so review quality drifts run to run. Not recommended as a reviewer.

quota.note: Zen free tier is enforced server-side with no queryable balance; failures show as 'Rate limit exceeded' in the opencode log (see og audit).

argv: Reply with exactly: ok. Do not use tools.
liveness.note: No action-enabling flags and a prompt that forbids tools: the probe is a capability check, not a dispatch. free_models is an exact-id allow-list of documented Zen free pins; a -free suffix alone is not evidence of a free model.

model.note: Under Omnigent agy does NOT pick its own model: with no pin the dispatched model resolves to null, the harness starts agy with no `--model`, and every dispatch dies on launch with `Runner disconnected unexpectedly` — a blank answer is a dead worker, not `let it choose`. `agy models` lists the lineup (gemini-3.8/3.7/3.6-flash-{high,medium,low}, gemini-3.1-pro-{high,low}, claude-*, gpt-oss-*). Prefer gemini-3.8-flash-medium: reviews are bounded and read-only, and the pro/high tiers take far longer to answer even a trivial prompt. Vendor follows the pinned model, exactly as the freebuff row says — a `claude-*` pin makes agy same-vendor with Claude Code for review purposes, so the registry's `vendor: google` no longer describes it.

install.note: Ships with the Antigravity editor; `agy` lands in ~/.local/bin.

model.note: Codex's subscription login already selects a default model, so a blank answer is fine. The CLI does not enumerate models, so this list is static — a newer id typed by hand is accepted (the picker offers to pin an unlisted id).

agents.label: Pi
agents.kind_note: `pi` is Omnigent's DIRECT Pi harness (not `pi-native`, the TUI wrap): Omnigent reports instruction_delivery COMPOSED_PER_TURN and subagents=False, so it receives every turn's prompt and is a leaf worker, never an orchestrator. `kind: direct` records that it has no vendor TUI — `og agents` Enter focuses its Omnigent view, not a CLI tab. The name is shared with the vendor binary on purpose; Omnigent resolves `pi` and `pi-native` from the same executable.

model.required_reason: Omnigent supplies no model for Pi; without a pin it falls back to its own saved or first authenticated model, which is not deterministic across providers.
model.note: Pi is MULTI-MODEL: it runs on whichever provider `omni setup` configured. A pin is REQUIRED because Omnigent supplies no model when `executor.model` is absent; Pi then falls back to its own saved or first authenticated model, which is not deterministic across providers and can silently run the wrong one. Pin an id THAT provider serves. The menu lists `pi --list-models`, Pi's own ambient catalog, as a starting point; it can include a provider other than the one Omnigent manages, so confirm the id is served by the provider configured with `omni setup` and type a different id if the menu does not have the right one. Vendor follows the pin when the id names a family (e.g. `deepseek/...`); an unplaceable pin is treated as UNKNOWN for the cross-vendor review check, because omni setup's provider is invisible to og. `multi` is only the mark/color key, never a claim that Pi is a distinct vendor.

quota.note: Pi owns no quota of its own: it runs on the provider configured with `omni setup`, so capacity and exhaustion messages belong to that provider. `og stats` reports unknown for this row rather than guessing a pool.

model.note: Cline ACCEPTS an ACP model switch it cannot serve instead of rejecting it. A wrong id yields 'completed' with an empty transcript and an untouched worktree — no error anywhere. Pin the id `cline auth` actually selected.

quota.note: Only meaningful with a DeepSeek API key in $DEEPSEEK_API_KEY; a Cline-account login has no public balance endpoint yet, so og stats reports unknown.

model.note: Kilo has no bare `auto`; it has an auto-ROUTER family — kilo/kilo-auto/{free,efficient,small,balanced,frontier} — plus kilo/openrouter/auto. `free` keeps it inside the free tier; the others bill at provider rates. Requires `kilo auth` first: an unauthenticated ACP worker fails silently with an empty transcript. An ACP session starts on Kilo's OWN default model (its last-used one, often paid) until the pin is applied; `Add credits to continue, or switch to a free model` means the pin never landed. Put `"model": "kilo/kilo-auto/free"` in ~/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc so even an unpinned session is free.

argv: Reply with exactly: ok. Do not use tools.
liveness.note: Runs only for the registry-listed free router; a paid pin is measured by kilo-profile and never liveness-probed.

agents.label: Kiro (AWS)
agents.kind_note: ACP rather than kiro-native on purpose. Omnigent's headless-worker seam (_derive_terminal_launch_args_from_spec) maps claude/codex/cursor/kimi/agy to their no-prompt flags but has no kiro-native entry, so a native Kiro worker asks for permission on every tool and depends on a tmux permission mirror that fails ('permission prompt was not safely focused before verdict delivery'). Over ACP, Kiro's own --trust-all-tools answers its prompts and permission_mode: bypassPermissions (acp-user) covers what it relays. Revisit once Omnigent maps kiro-native.

model.note: `auto` is Kiro's own default router (1.00x credits, model chosen per task). Over ACP the pin reaches Kiro as the session model (HARNESS_ACP_MODEL); unpinned uses Kiro's default, which is `auto` anyway. Free plan is 50 credits/month from the shared Kiro pool — overflow capacity, not a primary implementer.

quota.note: 50 credits/month on the free plan; no public remaining-credit endpoint found.

argv: Reply with exactly: ok. Do not use tools.
liveness.note: Probe only runs on a verifiably free pin; Kiro's `auto` default is not marked free, so it reports skipped.

model.note: Omnigent always launches `cursor-agent --model <id>`; with no pin the id is the ORCHESTRATOR's (e.g. claude-opus-5[1m]), which cursor-agent rejects (`Cannot use this model`) and exits 1 -- the pane dies before the first prompt and every dispatch reports `Harness stream connection error`. `auto` is Cursor's own router; `cursor-agent models` lists the rest.

install.note: See the Hermes docs for your platform.

agents.label: Grok Build
agents.kind_note: NOT an orchestrator: Omnigent reports harness `grok` subagents=False, so it cannot dispatch a sub-agent. The row used to claim `relay: true` AND list `orchestrator`, which would have built a brain that could never delegate.

model.note: Omnigent's builtin ACP rows own their auth and model selection (OWN_AUTH); a model override is rejected up front rather than silently dropped.

agents.label: Devin
agents.roles_note: `orchestrator` is MEASURED-capable: Omnigent reports harness `devin-native` subagents=True (the native Devin harness mirrors its in-TUI `run_subagent` calls as Omnigent child sessions), and `prompt_delivery` is not `none`, so it clears the orchestrator gates. The row used to point at a harness id `devin` that has no capability entry at all -- the preflight map would have dropped the worker; `devin-native` is the real id. UNVERIFIED as an orchestrator: no og run has been driven with devin as the brain. Demote to `coder` if the first real dispatch cannot orchestrate.

agents.label: Freebuff
agents.kind_note: `blink` (github.com/jmvbambico/bufflink, >= v0.1.2) is an ACP bridge that drives the freebuff TUI in a PTY. Verified 2026-09-20/21 in og-sandbox: five backlog tasks (small to larger, incl. new modules and e2e tests), 3 of 3 first-try since v0.1.2; every commit in scope, gates green. Facts that matter: one blink process = one freebuff launch = one hour billed up front at the chosen model's rate (GLM 5.3 Flash 5/hr by default, up to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 15/hr) from the free tier's 25 daily Freebucks, so a costlier pin means fewer launches per day, and the process lives as long as the sub-agent SESSION. Omnigent's sys_session_close does NOT end it (observed 2026-09-21): after closing a finished session, `pgrep -x blink` and SIGTERM it - blink exits cleanly within ~5 s and releases freebuff's single-instance lock; verify with `pgrep -fl manicode/freebuff` before the next launch. freebuff writes its transcript only at turn end, so nothing streams while it thinks; all trial turns finished well inside HARNESS_ACP_PROMPT_TIMEOUT_S (300 s), but keep tasks single-purpose. Omnigent's injected system prompt (~5 kB) arrives as a collapsed 'Pasted text' chip, which blink handles; leave inject_system_prompt on. freebuff resolves RELATIVE paths against the cwd omnigent passed (the workspace, not the worktree): dispatch text must use absolute worktree paths and name the gate commands with `cd`. freebuff writes `.freebuff/project-id` into its cwd; gitignore `.freebuff/`. No approval gate: freebuff runs commands unattended - the worktree is the blast radius. freebuff's model lineup ROTATES server-side and is served under provider-prefixed or hashed ids, so the picker's `choices` are a FALLBACK only: at setup time `blink --list-models` probes the live catalog and every id it prints is offered instead. Install a blink that speaks `--list-models` (>= v0.2.0); an older blink silently falls back to `choices`.

model.note: At setup time og runs `blink --list-models` and offers every id it prints; that live probe is the source of truth because the lineup ROTATES server-side. `choices` below is a FALLBACK used only when the probe fails or an older blink lacks `--list-models` -- never an empty list. Model ids are provider-prefixed or opaque hashes (e.g. `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, `mimo/mimo-v2.6-pro`, `openai/gpt-6-luna`, `upstage/solar-pro4`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, `m-79293c5b7d`), so a pin is always written with its prefix and never matched against a splash display name. Pinning one exports BLINK_MODEL=<id> into the worker env; a blink that honours BLINK_MODEL selects it, an older blink accepts freebuff's default. A pin naming a model freebuff is not offering fails the dispatch loudly rather than running the default. Vendor follows the model: a deepseek/* pick makes Freebuff same-vendor with Cline for review purposes. The HOURS ECONOMY is why a fallback pin is worth configuring: each launch draws from freebuff's small DAILY pool of hours at the pinned model's per-hour rate, so a costly pin can exhaust the pool and every later dispatch is refused with 'not enough Freebucks'. The picker's `unlimited` section is genuinely FREE (price_per_hour 0), so og probes the JSON catalog (`list_cmd_json`) for the free, id-mapped models and, after the pin is chosen, offers a SECOND free-only picker; the choice is exported as BLINK_FALLBACK_MODEL alongside BLINK_MODEL, and blink falls back to it when the pin is unusable. A blink too old to accept the variable ignores it, so leaving BLINK_FALLBACK_MODEL unset is always safe.
model.fallback_note: A free model (price 0) used only when the pinned model is unusable for quota/hours reasons. The picker's `unlimited` section is genuinely free, so it never draws on the paid hours pool. Optional: leaving it unset changes nothing, and an older blink that does not read BLINK_FALLBACK_MODEL ignores it.
model.list_cmd_json_note: The `--json` probe is the ONLY source of per-model prices: the plain listing prints bare ids with no price, so free models (price_per_hour 0) are discoverable from this JSON form alone. Entries whose `id` is null could not be mapped to a pinnable id and are dropped; `price_per_hour` null means a paid model with no printed per-hour figure, not free. Run only for the fallback picker, so setup for agents without a fallback is not slowed down.

quota.note: freebuff.com exposes no usable quota API (the subscription endpoint returns the SPA); og reports the balance freebuff itself last printed — in chat.db transcripts and runner logs — and unknown when nothing has reported since the daily reset. It never subtracts: freebuff bills per hour at a per-model rate (GLM 5.3 Flash 5/hr, MiMo 2.5 10/hr, Solar Pro 4 10/hr, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 15/hr), so a launch's cost depends on its model and duration. blink fails fast with 'not enough Freebucks' when the pool is empty.

agents.label: Command Code
agents.kind_note: `cmd-acp` (npm, v0.2.0, ~9 commits, last published 2026-08-06, fork of soycanopa/cmd-acp) bridges ACP to `cmd -p`, spawning one `cmd -p` process per prompt. It exposes model, reasoning effort and permission mode ONLY through the ACP method session/set_config_option, which Omnigent never sends (the acp_command docstring in og_install.py traces the wire). Its session config therefore starts EMPTY: no --model and, critically, no --yolo. Headless runs still go through Command Code's permission engine, so without --yolo the worker returns end_turn having changed nothing — the 'completed with no output' signature. The bridge does honour the env var CMD_BIN to choose the binary it spawns (dist/index.js, resolveCmdBinary), and passes the parent env through to it. That is why og points CMD_BIN at a generated shim instead of patching or forking the bridge. --tools-all is needed because headless runs withhold some tools; --skip-onboarding is needed because Command Code otherwise runs a taste-onboarding step on first launch. Setting permissions.defaultMode = yolo in ~/.commandcode/settings.json is the alternative to the shim, but it applies globally to the user's interactive cmd too and cannot carry --tools-all. The shim keeps it per-worker. Unlike freebuff/blink there is no long-lived process to reap: each prompt is one `cmd -p` that exits. Verified 2026-09-24 by driving cmd-acp over ACP stdio on a subscribed, authenticated account: with plain cmd-acp (no shim) the agent answered "I can't complete this — file writes are blocked", returned stopReason `end_turn`, and left the worktree untouched — the silent no-op this note predicts is real, and the proof the shim's --yolo is load-bearing rather than a precaution. WITH CMD_BIN pointed at the generated shim and CMD_MODEL=moonshotai/kimi-k3 it ran write_file and the file appeared with the requested contents; the shim fix works. cmd's OWN default model, read from the bridge's `session/new` response (`configOptions` -> model -> `currentValue`), is `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`: an UNPINNED cmdcode worker therefore runs DeepSeek and is silently same-vendor with Cline for cross-vendor review purposes — exactly why `model.required` is true and `silent_model_failure` is true. Command Code writes a `.commandcode/` directory into the cwd it is given (the worktree), the same way freebuff writes `.freebuff/`; gitignore `.commandcode/` or it turns up in every worker's diff.

model.note: (a) ids are provider-prefixed for open-weight models (moonshotai/…, deepseek/…, z-ai/…) but BARE for Anthropic and OpenAI (claude-sonnet-5, gpt-5.5); (b) vendor MUST follow the pinned model, exactly as the freebuff row says — pinning deepseek/* makes this same-vendor with Cline, z-ai/* same-vendor with Freebuff, meta/muse-spark-* same-vendor with OpenCode's pin, and claude-*/gpt-* same-vendor with the orchestrator and reviewer; the default moonshotai pin is chosen because no other roster member uses that vendor; (c) an unpinned run is a SUCCESSFUL cmd invocation on cmd's own default model, which is why silent_model_failure is true.

quota.note: Command Code enforces a rolling 5-hour AND a rolling weekly credit window, both rolling from first use, on top of the monthly credit pool (Go $1/$10, GOAT $10/$70, Pro $20/$80, Max 10x $100/$150, Max 20x $200/$300; Pro's windows are $16 per 5h and $40 per week). No queryable quota API. Exhaustion prints `You've reached your 5-hour usage limit. Resets in 2h 41m` — match that string to mark the worker dry and take --until from it.

argv: Reply with exactly: ok. Do not use tools.
liveness.note: No --yolo/--tools-all: a text-only probe needs no permissions, and the strict prompt is the guard against file writes. Paid pins are skipped, so this argv only runs on a future verified-free Command Code model.

$multiplexers: Catalog of terminal multiplexers og can drive. Same rule as `agents`:
adding one is a ROW here, not a working backend. A row buys DETECTION and
LISTING only -- the PATH scan, --check and --questions pick it up from the
row. Driving a multiplexer still needs BACKEND CODE behind it, exactly as
an agent row needs a harness plugin; do not read a row as evidence that a
backend exists.
Fields:
id            stable key
label         what --check and the picker show
binary        what the PATH scan looks for
url           where to get it (shown when it is missing)
session_unit  what a run's top-level session is called in this
multiplexer (herdr: a workspace)
worker_unit   what a dispatched worker's pane is called (herdr: a tab)
capabilities  the contract a backend for this multiplexer must meet. A
consumer may rely on ONLY what is listed. `agent_status`
(report whether a pane's agent is working or idle) is listed
because herdr has it and a future tmux backend would not,
which is exactly why it is enumerated rather than assumed.
verified      the version this row was last checked against, or false.
tmux is deliberately NOT listed: there is no tmux backend and `og start
tmux` does not exist, so a row would claim a capability that is not there.
The README names tmux as not-built, which is the honest place for it.

$prompt_delivery.argv: Prompt is appended to the CLI argv at startup. Subject to the tmux command-string ceiling (PROMPT_CEILING).
$prompt_delivery.per_turn: Prompt is composed and sent per turn over the harness's own transport. No command-line ceiling.
$prompt_delivery.first_user: Prompt is prepended to the first user message.
$prompt_delivery.none: The harness NEVER receives the spec prompt. A worker on this harness only ever sees the dispatch text, so operating rules must be inlined into args.input by the orchestrator. Cannot be an orchestrator.
$prompt_delivery.unknown: Not declared by Omnigent (user-configured ACP). Assume the prompt may not arrive; inline critical rules in the dispatch.

$quota.description: Optional per-agent `quota` blocks drive `og stats` (see docs/STATS.md). `probe` is the stats-layer probe name; it is null when the limit is known but exposes no queryable API, so `og stats` reports it as unknown rather than guessing. `daily` is the pool size consumed by the launch-budget probe (freebuff); that probe reports the balance freebuff itself last printed and never subtracts a per-launch cost.
